question: Should requester-scoped MCP become a public plugin SDK contract only after conflicting resolver claims disable that server, with the documented five-minute revocation window and shared-transcript boundary accepted?
rationale: The remaining issue determines which plugin may receive requester credentials and defines permanent public API, revocation, and conversation-visibility guarantees; automation cannot choose those authorization semantics safely.

options.title: Fail closed and approve
options.body: Disable requester resolution for any server with conflicting plugin owners, retain the documented timing and transcript boundaries, then rerun focused and live exact-head proof.

options.title: Accept first-registration wins
options.body: Explicitly support first-registration-wins ownership and accept that plugin activation order selects the resolver when server-name claims conflict.

options.title: Defer the public seam
options.body: Pause the PR and design resolver ownership together with broader requester identity, cron, subagent, and MCP scoping contracts.

recommendation.title: Fail closed and approve
recommendation.body: Disable requester resolution for any server with conflicting plugin owners, retain the documented timing and transcript boundaries, then rerun focused and live exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available feature-history signal is ownership of the session MCP runtime and tests whose lifecycle, cache keys, and authorization partition this decision changes.
